approved: Renewable Energy (Electricity) Amendment (Cheaper Home Batteries) Bill 2022
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would let homeowners earn certificates for installing home batteries, reducing the upfront cost.
It works by adding home batteries to the list of technologies that can create small-scale technology certificates under the existing renewable energy scheme.
Home batteries would create certificates for 15 years, but only if installed by 2030.
Adds home batteries as an eligible technology for small-scale technology certificates.
Extends the existing scheme for creating and trading certificates to cover home batteries.
Requires a ministerial review of the scheme's operation, with a final report due by 1 January 2029.
Householders and small businesses that install home batteries.

The bill would make home battery installations eligible for small-scale technology certificates under the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme, subsidising batteries to increase uptake, reduce power bills and grid volatility, and potentially add $7.4 billion and 35,000 jobs by processing battery materials domestically. The speaker noted over three million solar panels installed nationally, 30% of households with solar projected to reach 50% by 2030, and only 33,000 home batteries installed last year, with a target of 500,000 by 2030.
